evals.prompt: Storyboard a stronger version of the current CODE QUEST quiz. Keep the Oracle instead of a town, make the wait for generated questions feel intentional, and give me a design brief plus an executable CODEQUEST.toml.
evals.expected_output: A linked quiz storyboard and valid schema-v2 manifest using trusted Oracle and quiz handlers, with mechanics, art requirements, and explicit implementation status.
expectations: Produces both a human-readable design brief and a CODEQUEST.toml manifest.
The manifest passes the bundled schema-v2 validator with game.type set to quiz and no town scene.
The storyboard links Oracle latency to explicit mechanics, feedback, and art requirements.
The brief clearly distinguishes implemented, configured, and proposed behavior.

evals.prompt: I want a CODE QUEST stealth game where you sneak through a dependency graph and refactor modules without alerting regression guards. Design the scenes, mechanics, and art plan, but check what game types CODEQUEST.toml actually supports before you edit it.
evals.expected_output: A complete conceptual design that identifies the unsupported runtime type, avoids writing invalid TOML, and proposes the smallest schema/engine increment needed.

evals.prompt: Our existing quiz storyboard needs an accessibility pass. Add a reduced-motion Oracle state, non-color-only answer feedback, and clearer retry behavior. Preserve existing IDs wherever possible and update both the brief and manifest.
evals.expected_output: An incremental, traceable revision that preserves stable IDs, updates mechanics and art requirements, and keeps all manifest references valid.

evals.prompt: Polish this CODE QUEST cartridge end to end. The best gameplay screen already looks good, but the credits, opening, menus, failure states, and level progression still feel like a prototype. Reuse repository template assets where possible, close every FSM state, and cover animation and sound as well as static art.
evals.expected_output: A whole-game polish pass that covers every reachable scene and distinguishes executable behavior, production metadata, available assets, and proposed runtime work.
expectations: Audits credits and every other reachable scene across static presentation, motion, sound, mechanical closure, and felt progression.
Finds possible loading, failure, held-input, back, replay, and terminal open states rather than checking reachability alone.
Defines perceptible beginning, middle, and end progression through at least two feedback channels beyond a level number.
Inventories real template assets and does not claim that manifest metadata dynamically loads them unless the repository contract supports it.
Keeps the brief and CODEQUEST.toml valid, linked, and honest about implemented versus proposed work.

evals.prompt: Audit the native 240x160 character-creation and quiz frames for polish. The action label looks vertically off-center, the hero seems low on its platform, a heading touches the first identity row, and a decorative divider cuts through answer copy. Fix the design and implementation contracts so these classes of issue are caught elsewhere too.
evals.expected_output: A native-composite layout audit and revision that measures usable interiors, visible-alpha support lines, static ornament bounds, worst-case glyph cells, and all sibling intersections instead of approving only outer panel containment.
expectations: Measures centered copy against the usable art interior on both axes rather than the decorative outer shell.
Anchors the character's visible alpha support point to the platform or floor line rather than using nominal sprite dimensions.
Checks every relevant sibling foreground pair and catches the heading-to-row intersection.
Composites worst-case answer text with the plate and keeps decorative dividers outside glyph and inter-glyph cells.
Adds executable regression evidence for the corrected native layout instead of documenting intent alone.

evals.prompt: Polish the quiz HUD and progression. Health is shown as generic stars, score and streak are bare numbers, and Datafall exposes collectible and hit counts without meaningful stages. Make the UI feel native to the Oracle theme and ensure every tracked quantity rewards or warns the player at explicit thresholds.
evals.expected_output: A themed instrumentation and threshold pass that replaces generic HUD notation, defines desirable directions and exact breakpoints for every visible metric, and verifies the native states immediately below, at, and above each threshold.
expectations: Replaces generic health and counter notation with legible Oracle-themed instruments that deliberately use the available HUD space.
Defines empty, intermediate, full, gain, and loss states through shape, fill, count, fracture, position, or concise labels rather than hue alone.
Inventories score, streak, health, collectible, hazard, and completion tracking with desirable direction, thresholds, staged reward or consequence, cap, and reset.
Makes score or streak thresholds mechanically meaningful instead of merely recoloring the same flat reward.
Adds executable evidence at values immediately below, at, and above the declared breakpoints and inspects the final 240x160 composites.
